articles.title: Give saved content a lifecycle beyond the inbox
articles.excerpt: “Read later” is a destination with no exit in many personal workflows. Every interesting link enters the same list, while useful references and abandoned intentions remain mixed together. For a saved-…
articles.body: “Read later” is a destination with no exit in many personal workflows. Every interesting link enters the same list, while useful references and abandoned intentions remain mixed together. For a saved-content product, a small lifecycle can make that collection easier to understand without requiring an elaborate filing system. Start with three decisions Let a new save enter an inbox. During review, the user can choose to keep it as reference, use it for an active purpose, or archive it. These are proposed workflow states, not judgments about the quality of the content. “Keep” means the item may be useful again. “Use” connects it with a current activity. “Archive” removes it from the active view while preserving the option to retrieve it later. A resource can change roles.

articles.title: How to Reduce Soft Declines (and When a Retry Will Actually Work)
articles.excerpt: Originally published on the RetryFix blog. A soft decline is a refused card charge where the issuer has not said the card itself is finished. The charge failed this time. The same card might still pay…
articles.body: Originally published on the RetryFix blog . A soft decline is a refused card charge where the issuer has not said the card itself is finished. The charge failed this time. The same card might still pay later, or the customer might need to do one specific thing first: add funds, authenticate, or use another payment method. A hard decline is the other case. This card cannot complete the charge, and another attempt on it will not collect. This page is the practical half: how to have fewer soft declines in the first place, and when a retry is worth running. Which codes are which, and the slice of failed payments a retry will never collect, is in hard declines vs soft declines .

articles.body: Artificial intelligence is moving beyond generating information. AI agents are being developed to monitor systems, coordinate workflows, interact with external services, and execute tasks with limited human intervention. Blockchain introduces another dimension to these capabilities: the ability to execute transactions and interact with decentralized applications through verifiable, programmable systems. However, connecting AI agents to blockchain networks requires more than providing wallet access or integrating a smart contract. Autonomous applications depend on continuous data availability, secure transaction authorization, predictable network performance, and reliable execution.

articles.title: Build a Web-Grounded AI Research Tool with DeepSeek Search and Fetch APIs
articles.excerpt: An AI answer can sound current while quietly relying on yesterday's knowledge. For a question like “What changed in this library this week?”, a model needs two separate abilities: discover relevant pa…
articles.body: An AI answer can sound current while quietly relying on yesterday's knowledge. For a question like “What changed in this library this week?”, a model needs two separate abilities: discover relevant pages and read the pages it found. Until recently, teams commonly assembled those pieces from separate search and extraction services, or delegated them to a framework whose behavior was difficult to inspect. On October 17, 2026, DeepSeek opened its in-house search engine through two direct APIs: Search returns structured web results, and Fetch retrieves one URL as Markdown. The listed price is $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests for each API. That is a fresh building block, not a complete research agent. This tutorial turns it into one small, inspectable Python command-line tool.

articles.title: Did a giant object collide with Earth to form the moon?
articles.excerpt: Known as the giant-impact hypothesis, this proposed event involves a collision between Earth and a hypothetical Mars-sized protoplanet astronomers call Theia.
articles.body: For as long as humans have watched the night sky, we have wondered about the moon , pondering everything from its alien appearance to its influence over phenomena on Earth such as ocean tides, climate stability, and even the natural rhythms of many organisms. Among the many questions we have about Earth's lone natural satellite, one remains preeminent: what are the moon's origins , and how long has it orbited Earth? Today, the leading theory among astronomers is that deep in our planet's past — perhaps within roughly the first 100 million years of solar system history — Earth collided with a planet-sized object, creating the moon within a period that may have been as short as just a few hours .

It took them just over 27 hours to take down the Ender Dragon in what is believed to be a world first. Of course, it’s not as simple as just turning up and firing arrows at the thing. To reach The End and defeat the Ender Dragon in Minecraft , there are a series of trials you have to complete. articles.body: A modder has used AI to put Middle-earth: Shadow of War’s Nemesis System inside Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption 2 . The enRage mod, created by nicklovin99, tracks how individual enemies feel about you. This works largely the same way as Shadow of War's much-loved Nemesis System, creating rivalries on the fly and disrupting the ranks of rival gangs. And, like the Nemesis System, enRage names every single NPC in the game. Some like you, some fear you, and some want you dead. It groups people by gangs, groups, and affiliations, so you’ve got the O’Driscoll Boys, Lemoyne Raiders, the U.S. Army, The Klan, the Wapiti people, the Bronte Family, the Murfee Brood, the Skinner Brothers, Van der Linde, and unaffiliated randoms. These are all tracked in a new menu.

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.

articles.body: Japan's mission to Mars is one of the most ambitious in spaceflight history. It aims to become the first spacecraft to return to Earth from Mars orbit, carrying with it the first-ever samples from the Red Planet system. The mission, known as Martian Moons eXploration (MMX), is a first-of-its-kind endeavor to study the origin of Mars' moons Phobos and Deimos. The robust undertaking includes a landing on Phobos to collect the samples — which will likely be the first from the Mars system to return to Earth — and a search for evidence that could shed light on events during the formation of the solar system billions of years ago. articles.title: Computer scientist Margaret Hamilton was a problem-solver for the ages (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: The world will miss Margaret Hamilton, the pioneering programmer who helped NASA land Apollo astronauts on the moon. But we will always have her example to inspire us.
articles.body: Dean Robbins is a journalist and children's author. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton , who died on Sept. 30 at age 90, played a key role in putting astronauts on the moon. She was a problem-solver extraordinaire, and it all started in early childhood. Considering the name "daddy longlegs" unfair to female arachnids, young Margaret decided to call half of them "mommy longlegs." Wondering why the neighborhood baseball players were all boys, she determined to join the team herself. As she grew up in the 1940s and '50s, Margaret noticed a similar problem with various professions. Why were doctors, judges and scientists almost always men?

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 18, 1963: France's Félicette Becomes the 1st Cat in Space! >^..^<
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. While the U.S. and Soviet Union were busy launching primates, dogs and humans, the French decided to join the space race by launching a cat. Félicette, a stray tuxedo cat from the streets of Paris, was a substitute for another cat named Felix, who somehow escaped on launch day. So Félicette went where no cat had ever gone before. She boarded a French Véronique AG1 rocket and soared 130 miles above the Earth before safely parachuting back down. Luckily Félicette made it home alive and well, unlike many of the other animal astronauts that flew during the space race. Félicette, the first cat to fly into space in October 1963, is seen her carrier pre-flight.

articles.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
articles.excerpt: A citizen science project is seeking volunteers to comb through NASA telescope data for telltale signs of the galaxy's hidden black holes.
articles.body: Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70. Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters , is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole , volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.

articles.title: 10 best places to see the 2027 total solar eclipse in Spain
articles.excerpt: From the Costa del Sol to whitewashed mountain villages, here are 10 of the best places in southern Spain to experience the Aug. 2, 2027 total solar eclipse.
articles.body: Spain is one of the easiest places in the world to experience the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . The so-called "eclipse of the century" first makes landfall in Andalucía, where totality will last up to 4 minutes and 40 seconds during mid-morning, with the sun comfortably high at around 38-42 degrees above the horizon in the eastern sky. Excellent roads, plentiful accommodation and Málaga's international airport make this an obvious alternative to North Africa and the Middle East. However, choosing where to watch requires some thought.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
